notes:
{畳|たたみ} is a traditional Japanese straw mat used as flooring. Made from woven ⟦{藺草|いぐさ}→藺草：28108_igusa⟧ (rush grass) over a rice straw core, tatami has a distinctive fresh, grassy scent when new.

MEASUREMENT:
The counter {畳|じょう} measures room size by the number of mats:
- ⟦{四畳半|よじょうはん}→四畳半：28109_yojouhan⟧: 4.5 mats (~7.3 sq m) — a small room
- ⟦{六畳|ろくじょう}→六畳：noentry⟧: 6 mats (~9.7 sq m) — standard bedroom
- ⟦{八畳|はちじょう}→八畳：noentry⟧: 8 mats (~13 sq m) — a spacious room

ETIQUETTE:
- Always remove shoes before stepping on tatami
- Avoid stepping on the ⟦{縁|へり}→縁：noentry⟧ (border/edging) of the mats
- Do not drag furniture across tatami

CULTURAL NOTE:
Tatami rooms (⟦{和室|わしつ}→和室：10437_washitsu⟧) are found in most traditional Japanese homes, inns (⟦{旅館|りょかん}→旅館：01049_ryokan⟧), and temples. They are associated with ⟦{正座|せいざ}→正座：10552_seiza⟧ (sitting on the knees), ⟦{布団|ふとん}→布団：01720_futon⟧ (futon sleeping), and the ⟦{茶道|さどう}→茶道：04451_sadou⟧ (tea ceremony).
